title: Choosing an integration method
rows: \(\int x^pdx=\frac{x^{p+1}}{p+1}+C\), \(p\ne-1\); valid real interval. \(\int dx/x=\ln|x|+C\), interval excludes 0.
\(\int e^x dx=e^x+C\); \(\int\cos xdx=\sin x+C\); \(\int\sin xdx=-\cos x+C\). Radians.
\(u=g(x)\), \(du=g\prime(x)dx\); rewrite every factor. Check by the chain rule.
\(\int u\,dv=uv-\int v\,du\). Choose an easier remaining integral; finish with C.
\(\int_a^buv\prime dx=[uv]_a^b-\int_a^bu\prime vdx\). Same variable and bounds.
FTC: continuous integrand on closed interval. Substitution: g continuously differentiable; f continuous over its image. Definite parts: u,v continuously differentiable.
Antiderivative: \(F\prime=f\) on interval. Definite result: \(F(b)-F(a)\). Initial value determines C. Numerical samples supplement identities.
Simplify → elementary pair → inner derivative match → useful parts split. Reinspect after each transformation. Domain, signs and units remain part of the calculation.
